newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica futures mkt sees 8 pct 96/97 volume growth.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica futures mkt sees 8 pct 96/97 volume growth.

text.p: The financial markets division of the South African Futures Exchange (Safex) expected an eight percent increase in index futures and options volumes in the 1996/97 financial year, it said in its annual report.

This followed a 2.8 percent decline in turnover in 1995/96 in equity-index futures and options, which contribute the lion's share of Safex's business, to 7.65 million contracts from 7.87 million the year before.
Safex runs a successful financial futures and options exchange and during the past year also launched a commodity futures division.
Safex said the fall in volume, which was most marked in June 1995, was partly due to the commissioning of the automated trading system (ATS) on May 31 last year.

"It has often been stressed that the ATS could cause a temporary decline in trade as some of the double counting is eliminated and members take time to come to terms with all of the facilities offered by the ATS," Safex said.

It said that up to 200 terminals had been connected to ATS, comprising dealers and back-office staff. Within three years it was planned to replace land lines with satellite communciations, so improving network reliability considerably, Safex said.

Mark Barnes, chairman of Safex and the Safex Clearing Company Ltd (Safcom), said the exchange would be looking in the 1996/97 financial year at the development of a currency futures market with the approval of the central Reserve Bank.
However, this had not been included in Safex's budget for the coming year.
